items.title: What is EXIT-CVD?
items.content: EXIT-CVD is a five-year European research project that aims to transform how cardiovascular disease is detected, monitored and treated. It brings together 42 public and private partners across 17 countries and is co-funded by the EU Innovative Health Initiative (IHI) and industry partners.

items.title: How do I join the study?
items.content:
Click the 'Join Study' button on the homepage and follow these steps:
1. Check that you are eligible to take part.
2. Read the Participant Information Sheet.
3. Sign an electronic consent form.
4. Set up a study account.
5. Connect your devices (Huawei D3 Watch, RADAR Active App, RADAR Passive App).

items.title: Am I eligible to take part?
items.content: You may be eligible if you are aged 18 or over and have been diagnosed with, or are at risk of, cardiovascular disease. You will also need a smartphone (Apple or Android) and be willing to wear a Huawei D3 Watch provided by the study.

items.title: What devices and apps will I need?
items.content:
The study uses three main tools:
1. **Huawei D3 Watch** - A wearable device for ambulatory blood pressure monitoring, heart rate, activity and sleep tracking.
2. **RADAR Active App (aRMT)** - A smartphone app for completing patient-reported outcome questionnaires.
3. **RADAR Passive App (pRMT)** - A smartphone app that passively collects sensor data from your phone.

items.title: What is the Huawei D3 Watch?
items.content: The Huawei D3 Watch is a smartwatch with a novel integrated oscillometric wrist blood pressure cuff. It enables ambulatory blood pressure monitoring alongside standard health tracking features such as heart rate, activity and sleep monitoring.

items.title: What data will the Huawei D3 Watch collect?
items.content:
The watch collects:
- Ambulatory blood pressure measurements
- Heart rate data
- Physical activity levels
- Sleep duration and quality

items.title: What does the RADAR Active App (aRMT) do?
items.content: The RADAR Active App sends you regular questionnaires about your health, wellbeing and symptoms. Your responses help the research team understand your cardiovascular health from your perspective.

items.title: What does the RADAR Passive App (pRMT) do?
items.content: The RADAR Passive App runs in the background on your smartphone and collects sensor data such as activity levels and environmental data. It does not access your personal messages, photos, or browsing history.

items.title: How is my data kept safe?
items.content: Your data is stored securely on encrypted servers and is pseudonymised, meaning your name is replaced with a code. The data is managed by King's College London on the RADAR-base platform and handled in compliance with the EU GDPR and applicable national data protection laws.

items.title: Who will have access to my data?
items.content: Your pseudonymised data will be accessible to the EXIT-CVD research team and authorised consortium partners for research purposes only. It will not be shared with your healthcare provider or used for any purpose other than research.

items.title: Can I withdraw from the study?
items.content: Yes. Your participation is entirely voluntary and you can withdraw at any time without giving a reason and without any effect on your medical care. Contact the study team at exit-cvd@kcl.ac.uk to withdraw.

items.title: Who can I contact if I need help?
items.content: You can contact the EXIT-CVD study team at [exit-cvd@kcl.ac.uk](mailto:exit-cvd@kcl.ac.uk).

items.title: I haven't received my verification code
items.content:
1. Check your junk/spam folder for an email from platform@sep.radar-base.net
2. The code expires after 1 hour. If it times out or doesn't arrive, go back to the "verify account" page and click "Resend code"

items.title: What is RADAR-base?
items.content:
RADAR-base is an open-source platform for the collection of health information from surveys, smartphones and wearable devices. It is managed by King's College London. For the EXIT-CVD study, Onsentia provides the platform infrastructure for data collection and remote monitoring.

You can find more information at [https://radar-base.org/](https://radar-base.org)
